page: UpCloud GPU-8xCPU-64GB-1xL40S is a KVM-hypervised virtual server configured with an AMD EPYC 9575F processor. It features 8 shared vCPUs with 8 physical cores and 1 thread per core running at 2.0 GHz, paired with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. The server includes a single NVIDIA L40S GPU from the Ada Lovelace family, equipped with 48 GB of VRAM. No local storage is bundled with this instance type, and it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals top-tier single-core CPU performance, with Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core scores placing in the top 10%. Multi-core performance for both Geekbench and stress-ng falls in the average range. Memory performance is strong, with Passmark memory scores in the top 25% and large-block read bandwidth reaching 178.06 GB/sec. For LLM inference, the system demonstrates strong to top-tier performance on smaller models, processing 135M model text generation at 448.64 tokens/sec. However, prompt processing for larger 70B models is a bottleneck, registering in the bottom 25% at 6.59 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers high GPU resource density relative to its shared CPU allocation, making it a viable option for workloads that require substantial VRAM but do not demand fully dedicated CPU cores. The combination of an NVIDIA L40S GPU and 64 GB of RAM makes this server type suitable for medium-scale LLM inference, image processing, and GPU-accelerated data science tasks. It is less suited for large-scale 70B parameter model prompt processing or workloads requiring high-speed local NVMe storage.
